value.hook: When reviewing OMP cwd, extension precedence or daemon-extension skew
value.title: Worktree seats load branch-local extensions

sections.name: body
sections.value:
OMP extension discovery must be reviewed end to end: the native provider's project-before-user order, the capability's name key and first-wins dedupe, then the loader's later realpath pass. Looking only at the loader can wrongly conclude that worktree and global copies both execute.

For PR #304 at 941b81ae99478578f8b7b058eefd1dc5cdb5a701, installed OMP 18.16.0 selected only the worktree's extension in an independent discovery-only probe. An isolated user extension directory linked main's copy; both were discovered but only the project copy survived. Changing the capability key to the path in memory exposed both copies. No extension factories or live seats were started.

Branch-local extension provenance is not compatibility admission. F113's PA digest compares reported tree ids with daemon build stamps, but does not compare extensions without tree metadata or unstamped daemons. Registration accepts metadata without a minimum-version handshake. A successful spawn does not prove a branch-local older extension implements newer daemon expectations.

When sweeping spawn guidance, include routes/skill.md as well as peer/delegate/pair and the orchestrator's build-configuration paragraph. The PR's changed canonical paragraph can be correct while an earlier sentence in the same file still states the old refusal.

Read-only review proof must distinguish exact-head CI, independent installed-runtime discovery, author-reported mutations and locally unavailable tests. The shared-build timeout in this review fired before cargo started; it is not a failed regression. Do not bypass another seat's build lock or install/symlink dependencies to fill a C25 proof gap.
